sections.h2: Where is Greenwich, CT, and how big is the town?
sections.html:
Greenwich is the southwesternmost town in both Connecticut and New England. It covers 67.2 square miles in total, of which 47.8 is land and 19.4 is water, so by area it is about twice the size of Manhattan.

It borders Port Chester and Rye Brook, and North Castle, in New York, Stamford to the east, and Long Island Sound to the south. The town also owns offshore islands, including Great Captain Island, which has the southernmost point in Connecticut and a lighthouse. A seller with waterfront property should ask about flood zones, since so much of the town's area is water.

sections.h2: What shaped Greenwich's history and housing?
sections.html:
Agents Robert Feake and Daniel Patrick bought the land from the Siwanoy people for the New Haven Colony in 1640, and the General Assembly declared Greenwich a township on May 11, 1665. General Israel Putnam made his escape from British forces there on February 26, 1779.

Population grew from 12,172 in 1900 to 33,112 in 1930 and reached 63,518 in 2020. Because growth came in waves, a seller may own anything from a colonial in the historic district to a mid-century house or a newer build, and the repair profile varies a great deal across those eras.

sections.h2: Which Greenwich neighborhoods should a seller know?
sections.html:
Greenwich is one taxing body made up of distinct sections. Wikipedia notes that the Census Bureau recognizes nine communities within the town, and three have their own post office names and ZIP codes.

  • Cos Cob, Old Greenwich and Riverside, each with its own postal name.
  • Byram, Glenville and Pemberwick.
  • Indian Field and Rock Ridge.
  • Central Greenwich around the municipal center.

Informal areas include Belle Haven, Back Country, Banksville, Mianus and Stanwich. Zip codes in town are 06830, 06831, 06870 and 06878.

sections.h2: What drives Greenwich's economy and housing demand?
sections.html:
Greenwich is a center for hedge funds and financial firms, thanks to its residential setting and nearness to Manhattan. Companies based in town include AQR Capital, Viking Global Investors, Silver Point Capital, Interactive Brokers, W. R. Berkley, XPO and Tudor Investment Corporation. Greenwich Hospital, Eversource Energy and the Brunswick School are other major institutions.

Because the work is concentrated in finance, buyers often arrive from New York and commute by rail. A trip to Grand Central takes about 50 minutes on the express and 60 on a local. Westchester County Airport is about 15 minutes by car, and LaGuardia roughly 35.

sections.h2: How do schools, roads and transit work in Greenwich?
sections.html:
The public system has eleven elementary schools, three middle schools (Central, Eastern and Western) and one high school. Wikipedia reports that roughly 25 to 30 percent of K-12 students attend private schools, a high ratio for Connecticut, including Brunswick School, Greenwich Academy and Greenwich Country Day School.

Interstate 95 crosses the southern end of town with four exits, 2 through 5, and Route 1 and the Merritt Parkway also pass through. Amtrak trains stop in Stamford, the neighboring city. If your house is within walking distance of one of the four rail stations, say so early in any conversation with a buyer.

sections.h2: What weather and water issues affect a Greenwich house?
sections.html:
Greenwich has a humid continental climate with mean daily highs from 35 degrees in January to 82 in July and about 50 inches of precipitation a year. Snowfall averages about 28 inches, and the area north of the Merritt Parkway gets noticeably more than the coast because the Sound moderates temperatures.

For a seller, that means coastal homes face water and insurance questions while inland, higher houses face winter wear on roofs and driveways. Ask your insurance agent about your specific lot.

sections.h2: How is Greenwich governed, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Greenwich is a single taxing body with three selectmen elected town-wide and a Representative Town Meeting of 230 unpaid members that must approve every budget. Each voter can pick only two of the three selectmen, which almost always produces a split board.

Fred Camillo serves as First Selectman, according to Wikipedia. The town runs its own public safety, with career firefighters plus eight all-volunteer fire companies, and a police department at 11 Bruce Place. Because all neighborhoods share one tax base, the tax collector is the single point of contact for payoffs.

sections.h2: What are Greenwich's beaches, islands and parks?
sections.html:
Greenwich has four town beaches on the Sound: Greenwich Point, Byram Beach, Island Beach and Great Captain Island. Access was long limited to residents, until the Connecticut Supreme Court ruled in Leydon v. Greenwich in 2001 and the town amended its policy for all four.

  • Binney Park, Bruce Park, Cos Cob Park and Byram Park.
  • Mianus River Park and the Babcock Preserve.
  • Calf Island, a 29-acre island about 3,000 feet off Byram, with a bird sanctuary on its west side.

The Bruce Museum is town-owned, and Putnam Cottage is a historic house museum.

sections.h2: How is a Greenwich sale recorded, and what does the state tax?
sections.html:
A deed cannot be recorded by the town clerk until the conveyance tax return is filed and the tax paid, under section 12-497. Section 12-494 sets the base at three-quarters of one percent for the state plus one-fourth of one percent for the town. For residential sales of $800,000 or more, the state rate steps up on the portion above $800,000, and again above $2.5 million.

The statute pages carry a note that the 2026 Supplement holds recent amendments, so have your closing attorney confirm the current figures.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale compare with listing in Greenwich?
sections.html:
Listing a Greenwich house can attract a wide pool of buyers, but a house needing work, or a sale with a deadline, may fit a cash buyer better. A cash buyer purchases as-is and does not depend on a lender's appraisal.

  • Listing: broader exposure, more showings, inspection requests.
  • Cash sale: simpler, driven by title work, usually at a discount to a renovated sale.

Get any offer in writing, and have your attorney review the contract before you sign.

faqs.q: Is Greenwich the largest town on the Gold Coast?
faqs.a: Wikipedia describes Greenwich as the largest town on Connecticut's Gold Coast, in southwestern Fairfield County, with a 2020 population of 63,518.

faqs.q: How long is the train from Greenwich to Manhattan?
faqs.a: Metro-North's New Haven Line takes about 50 minutes to Grand Central on the express and about 60 on the local.

faqs.q: Do I pay conveyance tax when selling a Greenwich house?
faqs.a: Connecticut taxes deeds of $2,000 or more, with higher state rates on residential sales above $800,000. Ask your closing attorney for the current figure.

faqs.q: How many public high schools does Greenwich have?
faqs.a: One. Greenwich High School is the district's sole high school, with three middle schools feeding it.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Greenwich house as-is for cash?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases the house in its current condition, with no repairs. Compare offers in writing and have a contract reviewed before signing.

faqs.q: What is the weather like in Greenwich, CT?
faqs.a: Greenwich has a humid continental climate. January highs average around 35 degrees, July highs about 82, and snowfall averages about 28 inches a year. The area north of the Merritt Parkway gets more snow than the coast.
